 Petrol, Diesel Prices Today, October 23: Check Latest Rates In Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru

 Mumbai, October 23 : Petrol and diesel prices today, October 23, remained unchanged across major Indian cities, including Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. Petrol costs Rs 102.12 per litre in New Delhi, while diesel is priced at Rs 95.20 per litre. Among the cities listed, Hyderabad has the highest petrol price at Rs 116.15 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram records the highest diesel rate at Rs 104.40 per litre.
 Crude oil prices rose in early Asian trading on Friday after surging 4% in the previous session to a five-month high, as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia heightened concerns over potential disruptions to global energy supplies.
 Brent crude futures rose 0.6% to $113.8 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude advanced 0.7% to $100.2 per barrel. Brent was on track to register its third consecutive weekly gain.
 Supply concerns intensified after Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran as fighting escalated between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthi militants. The group has advanced towards Bab el-Mandeb, a strategic shipping chokepoint at the entrance to the Red Sea, raising fears of further disruption to energy shipments.
 Adding to supply pressures, the shutdown of an oil pipeline valve in Libya reduced production at the Hamada and Tahara oilfields, according to the country’s National Oil Corporation. Meanwhile, the prospect of renewed US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine offered a potential diplomatic development, although sanctions on Russian energy exports continued to support oil prices.
 For India, elevated crude prices remain a concern given the country’s dependence on imported oil. A prolonged rally could increase the import bill, exert pressure on the rupee and add to inflationary risks, while squeezing margins for fuel retailers and raising costs for oil-dependent industries.
 Check the latest city-wise petrol and diesel rates across metro cities and state capitals.
 Petrol Prices 
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Friday, with New Delhi recording a rate of Rs 102.12 per litre. In the National Capital Region, petrol was priced at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurgaon and Rs 101.96 per litre in Noida, with no daily change reported.
 Among the metropolitan cities, Kolkata had the highest petrol price at Rs 113.51 per litre, followed by Mumbai at Rs 111.21 per litre, Bengaluru at Rs 111.68 per litre and Chennai at Rs 107.76 per litre. All four cities reported no change in petrol prices.
 Among other state capitals, Hyderabad recorded the highest rate at Rs 116.15 per litre, followed by Thiruvananthapuram at Rs 115.49 per litre. Petrol was priced at Rs 113.37 per litre in Patna, Rs 113.19 per litre in Jaipur and Rs 108.97 per litre in Bhubaneswar.
 Chandigarh had one of the lowest petrol prices among the cities listed, at Rs 101.54 per litre, followed by Lucknow at Rs 101.86 per litre. With prices unchanged across all the listed locations, motorists saw no immediate relief or additional burden at fuel stations. City-wise rates may vary depending on local taxes and other pricing components.
 Diesel Prices 
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Friday, with New Delhi recording a rate of Rs 95.20 per litre. In the National Capital Region, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurgaon and Rs 95.44 per litre in Noida, with no daily revision reported.
 Among the metropolitan cities, diesel cost Rs 99.82 per litre in Kolkata, Rs 97.83 per litre in Mumbai, Rs 99.55 per litre in Chennai and Rs 99.56 per litre in Bengaluru. Prices remained steady across all four cities.
 Among other state capitals, Thiruvananthapuram recorded the highest diesel price at Rs 104.40 per litre, closely followed by Hyderabad at Rs 104.23 per litre. Diesel was priced at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar, Rs 99.36 per litre in Patna and Rs 98.25 per litre in Jaipur.
 Chandigarh recorded the lowest diesel price among the listed cities at Rs 89.47 per litre, followed by Lucknow at Rs 95.36 per litre. With no changes reported across the cities covered, diesel prices remained stable for consumers. Rates vary from city to city because of differences in local taxes and other pricing components.
